description: Shared Renovate preset for the HomeFlare fleet (taslabs-net). Consumed per-repo via extends: ["github>taslabs-net/renovate-config"].

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fix PRs from GitHub's Dependabot alerts (alerts stay on; Dependabot's own fix PRs are off). Renovate applies this block as a forced override, so a plain packageRule cannot regroup it: the shared branchTopic below keeps the vitest family on ONE branch, and the vitest <5 allowedVersions packageRule still applies because GitHub-alert rules only set matchCurrentVersion. osvVulnerabilityAlerts is deliberately NOT enabled: OSV fix rules force allowedVersions to the fixed version and would bypass the vitest cap. ⚠️ The block is applied as `force` (Renovate init/vulnerability.js), so no packageRule can re-hold it: a GitHub-alert fix for a held family (vitest, alchemy, effect, bun, payload, the ct100 obs images) is labelled lander:eligible and automerges once checks are green. A security fix outranks the hold on purpose; deploy-approve still verifies the alchemy/effect pair before any deploy.

customManagers.description: homeflare-ct100 declares each obs image twice: in the props (src/alertmanager.ts, victoria-*.ts, vmagent.ts, reconcile/grafana.ts, reconcile/vmalert.ts) and in the byte-exact live copy src/obs-render/<name>.container, which the quadlet manager already tracks. Renovate edited only the copy, so tests/reconcile-render.test.ts failed on every bump (ct100 PRs 485, 486, 487, 492, 538). This manager edits the props too; same depName and version, so one branch. The file patterns match nothing in any other repo. Add a file only when its tests do not hardcode the tag or digest.

packageRules.description: homeflare-ct100: src/obs-render/*.container is the byte-exact copy of the live Quadlet, and tests/reconcile-render.test.ts renders it from the props, so a fixture-only bump can never pass. Images the ct100 regex manager above does not cover (forgejo, openwebui, paperless, the exporters, unpoller) are bumped by hand with their props and tests; extend that manager's file list instead of removing this rule.

homeflare-ct100: these images run live on CT100 (the obs plane). A merge changes the declared image and the next deploy restarts the unit onto it, so none automerges: read the upstream notes and plan the deploy.

Vendored content is never edited. homeflare-os packages/artifacts-ci/os-core-lock/** is an upstream workspace kept only for its lockfile (its workspace:* members are absent, so every pnpm artifact update there fails, measured 2026-10-21). Vendored charts (homeflare-proxmox talos/charts/**) are verbatim helm pulls pinned by a tree digest and a provenance list, so a Renovate edit to a file under them can never pass check; a bump is a re-pull plus re-pin in one reviewed change. A packageRule on the file path, not ignorePaths: ignorePaths would replace the :ignoreModulesAndTests defaults that config:best-practices sets.

config:best-practices includes :pinDevDependencies. Those range pins were immortal, automerge stayed off, and renovate/artifacts failed, so the queue filled with pin PRs that could not land. Digest pins for Docker stay.

GitHub Actions digest pins stay off: .github/workflows/* is rendered by @homeflare/config's repo-shape (the fleet-wide pin point), so a pinDigest edit lands in generated files and fails the repo-shape drift test. Bump the action reference in @homeflare/config instead.

Third-party release age by update type: config:best-practices already waits 3 days for every npm update (security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm) and this preset extends the same for PyPI, so a patch waits 3 days; a minor or major waits 7. Only npm and PyPI: their NAS cache lookups keep the publish timestamp, while the docker distribution proxies and the Go proxy path give none or none checked, and minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour timestamp-required would hold those updates forever. The first-party kit rule below sets null and wins.
bun/npm: group minor+patch, automerge on green.
GitHub Actions: group minor+patch+digest, automerge on green.
Docker / Dockerfile / compose: group minor+patch+digest, automerge on green.
Python: group minor+patch across the package managers the fleet uses, automerge on green.
psycopg and psycopg-binary release together. Their own group, so a binary bump cannot land apart from the library.
Go modules: group minor+patch, automerge on green. A module xcaddy rewrites still fails its check and stays for a person.
golang.org/x moves as one module family.
google.golang.org, including grpc and genproto, moves as one module family.
OpenTelemetry Go modules release together.
Caddy and its security handler. One group. xcaddy regenerates builds/caddy/go.mod, so a bump that does not match that output fails the check and is not automerged.
Model Context Protocol packages share one version train.

Majors are never automerged; they want reading. A third-party major is not even proposed until someone ticks it on the Dependency Dashboard (dependencyDashboardApproval), and it carries the lander hold label, so a green major still waits for a person to remove hold. A GitHub security alert is the exception: the vulnerabilityAlerts block forces approval off and lands it once required checks are green. The first-party kit rule below turns approval back off for @homeflare/*.
vitest family moves as ONE group: vitest, @vitest/* and @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers. Splitting them breaks peers (pool-workers pins vitest's major). Never automerged.
Hold vitest + @vitest/* at the major @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers supports (its peer is vitest ^4.1 as of 0.23.0). Raise this cap only when a pool-workers release widens its vitest peer range.
Upstream tracker: Payload CMS. payload and @payloadcms/* release in lockstep (the estate runs the 4.0 canary line), so they move as ONE group; never automerged.

Upstream tracker: Cloudflare Workers toolchain. wrangler, miniflare, @cloudflare/workers-types, @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider and @cloudflare/vite-plugin move together. @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers stays in the vitest group, which owns its peer cap. A non-major automerges once checks are green. A major stays a pull request.
Upstream tracker: Alchemy (the estate runs the 2.0 beta line) and its distilled SDKs. One group, never automerged: a beta bump can change resource behaviour.
Upstream tracker: Effect. effect and @effect/* share one version train; split bumps break peers. A non-major in this group automerges once checks are green. A major stays a pull request.

HOLD: effect pinned to exactly 4.0.3 fleet-wide (the effect resolution alchemy 2.0.0-beta.81's anchors were verified against — landscape scripts/deploy-approve/env.ts VERIFIED_EFFECT_VERSIONS). 4.0.4+ changes Effect's requirements type parameter so `Effect<A, E, any>` no longer assigns to `Effect<A, E, never>`, which fails `tsc` in homeflare-landscape (scripts/memory/api.ts, scripts/seats/bundles/sdk-port.ts) and would fail deploy-approve's effect-layer check. Lift only after a newer effect passes the effect-layer review and VERIFIED_EFFECT_VERSIONS gains that resolution.
Upstream tracker: Bun runtime and its types (npm, packageManager/engines, and the oven/bun image) move as one.

HOLD: Bun runtime pinned to exactly 1.4.0 fleet-wide (Tim 2026-10-14). In Bun 1.4.2, a process that installs a SIGTERM or SIGINT handler exits 143 and its cleanup never runs, so seed and cleanup tests fail and pre-push hooks block. 1.4.0 is verified good. Covers packageManager, engines, setup-bun bun-version and the oven/bun image. @types/bun is type-only and is not held. Lift this only after a newer Bun passes homeflare-openbao's SIGINT/SIGTERM seed tests.

Upstream tracker: vite and @vitejs/* move together, because @vitejs/plugin-react majors require a matching vite major (plugin-react 6 needs vite ^8). Grouped instead of held, so both move at once. A non-major automerges once checks are green. A major stays a pull request.

Upstream tracker: Flue. @flue/* move as one group. Excludes 2.0.4 only, a known broken publish (homeflare pnpm-workspace.yaml); every other version is allowed. A non-major automerges once checks are green. A major stays a pull request.

builds/caddy/go.mod is what xcaddy writes from builds/caddy/build.ts (Caddy stays at the measured 2.11.4). A module bump in that file is rewritten back and the check fails. Bump the catalog in build.ts instead.

First-party kit. One group per repo, a one-hour soak instead of the third-party release age, no dashboard approval, prPriority 10 (created before any other pull within the per-repo limits), and not held to the host schedule. Automerges once required checks are green. Tim wants the fleet bump fast (2026-10-21); the soak is the Opus round-1 fix: the kit repo is private, so npm provenance is off and a rogue or broken publish is otherwise on every consumer within minutes, and a @homeflare/config refresh rewrites the CI workflow that grades it. The canary rule below takes a release at once, so a bad one shows red there first; a hold for a bad version is one allowedVersions commit here. This rule wins the major ban; the kit-major rule after it holds majors. The @homeflare/config refresh rule does not set automerge.

Lock-file maintenance sorts last and only runs in the Monday-morning window, so with one new pull per repo per hour it could slip behind the backlog for weeks (Opus round 2). prPriority 5 puts it after the kit (10) and before everything else.

Kit canary: homeflare-wiki takes every @homeflare release with no soak, so a broken release goes red there inside the hour the rest of the fleet waits. Pick a canary with a real ci and no deploy of its own.

Kit majors are proposed with the kit group's speed but held: a breaking kit change lands only when a person removes hold (or, in lander mode, through the lander with its own gates). ⚠️ INERT WHILE THE KIT IS 0.x (every @homeflare package today): Renovate classifies 0.36 -> 0.37 as minor (lookup/update-type.js), so this matches nothing until a package reaches 1.0. 0.x minors landing after the soak is the deliberate fast-track (Tim 2026-10-21); the soak, the canary and the allowedVersions kill switch are its guard, not this rule.

After @homeflare/config is bumped, install that lockfile and refresh the rendered repo shape in the same commit. The command string is RENOVATE_REPO_SHAPE_REFRESH in homeflare-mini; the admin allowlist matches it and nothing else. A repo with no repo-shape:refresh script exits 0. This rule does not set automerge, so the kit rule above still wins the major ban.

homeflare-kit publishes exact dependency versions that must equal the root catalog. After a bump, copy those versions into catalog. The command string is RENOVATE_CATALOG_SYNC in homeflare-mini; the admin allowlist matches it and nothing else. A repo with no catalog exits 0.

commands: node --eval 'const fs=require("fs");const text0=fs.readFileSync("package.json","utf8");const root=JSON.parse(text0);if(!root.catalog)process.exit(0);let text=text0;for(const dir of fs.readdirSync("packages")){const path="packages/"+dir+"/package.json";if(!fs.existsSync(path))continue;const deps=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path,"utf8")).dependencies||{};for(const [name,version] of Object.entries(deps)){if(!(name in root.catalog))continue;if(typeof version!=="string"||version.startsWith("workspace:")||version.startsWith("catalog:"))continue;if(root.catalog[name]===version)continue;const from=JSON.stringify(name)+": "+JSON.stringify(root.catalog[name]);const to=JSON.stringify(name)+": "+JSON.stringify(version);if(!text.includes(from))process.exit(1);text=text.split(from).join(to);root.catalog[name]=version}}if(text!==text0)fs.writeFileSync("package.json",text)'

packageRules.description: Valkey stays on 8.1.x until a deliberate move: the CI job image's Valkey must match the live Valkey (homeflare-mini src/ci-runner/image/Dockerfile, ONE DECLARED VALKEY). Renovate PR 297 in homeflare-mini bumped it to 9.x on 2026-10-19 and broke every fresh job-image build. A major Valkey move is a planned change, not a bump.
